items.title: 🇧🇷🇺🇸 Reuters: Brazilian intelligence officials briefed French and German officials in September on alleged U.S. and Russian interference ahead of Brazil’s presidential election. Brazil’s Abin spy agency alleged U.S. interference ranging from “lawfare” to openly acknowledged political involvement, but provided no details about alleged Russian activity. The U.S. has denied trying to interfere, while Russia has previously denied meddling in foreign elections.

Más avanzados estaban los planes para asesinar a Ilya Ponomarev, él único diputado ruso que votó contra la anexión de Crimea y que desde el exilio ha colaborado sobre el terreno con la defensa armada de Ucrania.
(En Vilna, dos exiliados rusos en la mirilla. Uno recibió protección cuando la red de asesinos se puso en marcha en 2024)
Un reclutado a las órdenes de Moscú filmó dos emplazamientos de una de las víctimas en EEUU, respondiendo a instrucciones precisas formuladas en clave: "medir terreno"= grabar, "construir"=matar. Cada tarea tenía un precio, pero no hubo acuerdo para la segunda.
@ElMundoInter

items.title: "Missile alerts are costing Ukraine an estimated $45m (£34m) for every hour they bring business to a halt, according to the country’s economy minister, as Kyiv searches for ways to keep the economy running under an intensifying Russian bombardment. Russia has increasingly targeted the infrastructure underpinning Ukraine’s economy, striking industrial sites, warehouses, logistics hubs and datacentres in what Oleksandr Kravchenko, the minister for economy and the environment, described as an effort to 'destroy pretty much the entire economy'. 'What we had not fully anticipated was how quickly Russia would develop these jet-powered drones and use them to target everything,' he said, referring to Russia’s use of the new weapons that have pounded Kyiv in recent weeks... The president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has recently put Ukraine’s remaining budget shortfall this year at about $27 bn, a figure that has prompted questions among some European governments over how the gap emerged, despite the EU having already agreed a €90bn loan package for Ukraine covering 2026 and 2027. Kravchenko said the government had since narrowed the shortfall to $20 bn through spending cuts and by identifying additional domestic reserves." https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/30/missile-alerts-cost-ukraine-businesses-halt

items.title: "Russia launched large-scale strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure on the night of 29-30 September. Source: Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi Quote: 'Since summer, there's barely been a day without an attack on our energy infrastructure. But a combined strike of this scale hasn't happened since the end of last heating season.' Details: A total of 11 regions across Ukraine have come under attack since the evening of Tuesday. Emergency repair work and efforts to deal with the aftermath of the attack are ongoing. Koretskyi added that local authorities must ensure backup power systems at critical facilities in their communities are ready for use and that all installation and connection work is completed as soon as possible. Background: As of the morning of Wednesday 30 September, some consumers in the city of Kyiv and Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Sumy and Kharkiv oblasts were without power as a result of hostilities and Russian attacks. https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/09/30/8055756/

items.title: "The U.S. awarded Sabena Aerospace Engineering, a Belgian company, a contract of up to some $235.5 million for maintenance of Ukraine’s F-16s, though subcontractors perform some of the work. Phase inspection generally takes two to six weeks in the U.S., but it’s 'taking as long as 40 weeks in Belgium,' says retired U.S. Navy Rear Adm. Mark Montgomery. Another Western source tells us that more than half of Ukraine’s F-16s are currently in maintenance limbo, and at the current pace of use and maintenance Kyiv will exhaust the rest by the end of the year. A Ukrainian air force spokesman declined to comment." https://www.wsj.com/opinion/ukraine-f-16-maintenance-delays-russia-sabena-engineering-85ca626a

items.title: RT by @RALee85: Based on the information collected by the Estonian Internal Security Service @kaitsepolitsei we can conclude with certainty that the arson attack on Milrem Robotics premises that took place on the night of 14–15 august in Tallinn was an act of sabotage ordered by the special services of the Russian Federation. Such actions are absolutely unacceptable. In response, the @MFAestonia will today summon Russia’s Chargé d’affaires. The perpetrators have been apprehended and no longer pose a threat to our national security. Estonia is a difficult environment for Russia to carry out such actions because we act decisively and swiftly to protect our state. This act of sabotage is part of Russia’s broader campaign across Europe, aimed at intimidating us and weakening our support for Ukraine. Our response will be the opposite. We will increase both our support for Ukraine and the pressure on Russia to end its aggression. Let’s not lose focus and stay the course, because Russia’s actions are a clear indication that our collective exertion of pressure is working.

items.title: “Russia plans to spend 17.1 trillion roubles ($202.58 billion) on defence in 2027, around 27% more than the 13.5 trillion roubles originally budgeted and the highest figure since the ‌start of the war in Ukraine in 2022, government documents seen by Reuters showed on Monday. Total defence spending will amount to 50 trillion roubles in the next three years, according to the documents. In 2026 the government planned to spend 12.1 trillion roubles on defence but the actual amount is classified ⁠and will not be disclosed. Some military spending can also be accounted for in other parts of the budget. The documents also showed the government raised its estimate for its 2026 budget deficit to 3.2% of gross domestic product, from 1.6% of GDP previously. Budget spending in 2026 will increase by 13.2% to 48.6 trillion roubles or 20.9% of GDP.” https://www.reuters.com/world/russia-raises-2027-military-spending-by-27-budget-documents-show-2026-09-28/

items.title: Despite the fact that the frontlines are still moving in this area, one thing can be said already: The third Battle of Lyman in this war is basically over and Ukraine won. Again. After eliminating most of the northern salient around Lyman, around 250 Russian soldiers were captured. This is substantial number given that in previous instances Russians were quite effective in running away. The number indicates that multiple Russian positions were overrun while many more were cut off. It is also likely that the southern salient of the Russian occupation is under pressure. It is likely that Russians will try it a fourth time, but an encirclement of this Ukrainian city in the Donetsk region is once more as far away as it was around one year ago. From an operational point of view this is a major setback for Moscow.
